articles.title: ‘Massive difference between words and actions’: Ex-India cricketer’s blunt take on Ravindra Jadeja’s snub
articles.summary: Former India opener Aakash Chopra has questioned the selectors’ decision to leave Ravindra Jadeja out of the entire five-match ODI series against New
articles.body: Former India opener Aakash Chopra has questioned the selectors’ decision to leave Ravindra Jadeja out of the entire five-match ODI series against New Zealand, pointing to what he sees as a contradiction between the team management’s stated plans and its selection choices.India are scheduled to play five ODIs against New Zealand, beginning in Auckland on November 4. Axar Patel has been preferred over Jadeja as the left-arm spin-bowling all-rounder, despite the Indian think tank previously indicating that Jadeja remains part of its plans for the 2027 World Cup.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Chopra said Jadeja’s absence had not received enough attention and questioned the credibility of the assurances given about the veteran’s future in the team."Ravindra Jadeja not being there is a big thing. Many people haven't spoken about it. You are playing him very little anyway. You said that he is an integral part of our team, that he is part of your 2027 World Cup plans, but it doesn't seem like that, because there is a massive difference being seen in what you say and what you do," he said.Chopra pointed out that Jadeja had featured against the West Indies but was not played in the third match of that series either. The all-rounder has now been left out of both the first three and the final two matches against New Zealand.The former India opener believes Axar may have moved well ahead of Jadeja in the race for a place in the squad for the 2027 World Cup, suggesting the selectors might already have settled on their preferred option."You played him against the West Indies just now, and you didn't play him the third match there either. Here, you have neither picked him for the first three matches nor the last two matches. Axar Patel has run so far ahead in this race that it seems like the selectors have made up their minds about Ravindra Jadeja," he observed.While acknowledging that Jadeja's white-ball numbers have declined, Chopra said the selection pattern appeared to indicate that India were gradually moving away from the experienced all-rounder. He, however, stopped short of declaring whether that was the right decision.Chopra questions Manav Suthar’s omission from Test squadJadeja was not the only selection decision that drew Chopra's attention. The former cricketer also questioned why left-arm spinner Manav Suthar had not been included in India's squad for the two-Test series against New Zealand.Chopra highlighted Suthar's impressive start to his international career, pointing out that the spinner had taken 23 wickets in his first three matches. He also recalled that Suthar was named Player of the Match in his debut game and had been India's leading bowler during the tour of Sri Lanka."Manav Suthar's name is not there. Let that sink in. He has a three-match career in total, in which he was the Player of the Match in the first match. He was the pick of the Indian bowlers in Sri Lanka," he said.Chopra acknowledged that Jadeja remained ahead of Suthar in the pecking order, but wondered whether the younger spinner could have been considered instead of Washington Sundar."I know only one of Jadeja or Manav Suthar can play, and Jadeja is ahead in that race, but you cannot ignore Manav Suthar's 23 wickets in three matches. Could his name have been there in place of Washington Sundar?" Chopra observed.The commentator also stressed that the selectors should speak to Suthar and explain why he had been overlooked after such a promising start. To underline the significance of his returns, Chopra compared taking 23 wickets in three Tests to scoring three hundreds in as many matches.India's ODI squads for New Zealand tourFirst three ODIs: Shubman Gill (C), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer (VC), KL Rahul (WK), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Anshul Kamboj, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Ishan Kishan (WK), Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna* and Kuldeep Yadav.Fourth and fifth ODIs: Shreyas Iyer (C), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Tilak Varma, Ishan Kishan (WK, VC), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Kumar Kushagra (WK), Mohammed Siraj, Yash Thakur and Kuldeep Yadav.India’s Test squad: Shubman Gill [C], Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul [VC], Devdutt Padikkal, Rishabh Pant [WK, availability is subject to fitness clearance], Dhruv Jurel [WK], Ravindra Jadeja, Anshul Kamboj, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep, Sai Sudharsan, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammed Siraj.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Armed with MS Dhoni’s advice, Kartik Sharma set for captaincy debut
articles.summary: Jaipur: When Kartik Sharma, a young wicketkeeper-batter from Bharatpur district, marked his guard on his red-ball debut two seasons ago, he announced his
articles.body: Jaipur: When Kartik Sharma, a young wicketkeeper-batter from Bharatpur district, marked his guard on his red-ball debut two seasons ago, he announced his arrival with authority. He slammed a blistering 115 off 113 balls against Uttarakhand in the Ranji Trophy 2024-25. That initial breakthrough set the tone for a domestic journey built on an unwavering appetite for runs.He truly became elemental to the chatter last year when his explosive six-hitting ability during pre-season trials caught the eye of various IPL franchises, culminating in a Rs14.20 crore contract with the Chennai Super Kings (CSK). Now, at just 20 years of age, he finds himself thrust with the bigger responsibility of leading the senior Rajasthan side. Following left-arm spinner Manav Suthar's departure to New Zealand for India ‘A’ duty, the young 'keeper-batter steps up to lead a side riding high on confidence, having secured three points via a crucial first-innings lead in their opener against Tamil Nadu in Group ‘D’ fixture.Speaking on the eve of the clash against Railways, Kartik opened up about taking over the captaincy reins and said, "I have captained Rajasthan during Under-19 days. I will try to make the team as comfortable as I can. There are a few seniors while most of them are my contemporaries in the side, so I will ensure I remain as humble with them as possible."Kartik’s gritty knock of 42 off 75 balls in the second innings against Tamil Nadu showcased a new dimension to his batting. He credits his high-stakes stint under CSK umbrella for sharpening his match awareness and instilling the patience required to play according to the situationA definitive piece of advice from franchise veteran MS Dhoni has shifted his approach away from brute force toward timing and technical precision. "When I went to Chennai I was a little injured and that is why my batting wasn't going very well. Bhaiya told me to focus on timing. He said that you aren't someone who hits power shots, whatever your timing is, that is your power, so play according to that,” he shared.Kartik has seamlessly integrated this sense of responsibility into his batting, balancing his natural boundary-clearing instincts with a refined technique. “Six-hitting is definitely there, but I am also working on grounded shots and doing my practice for that," he added.Addressing the composition of a dressing room that is decidedly youthful, Kartik sees the clean slate as a strength rather than a setback. "Nothing negative, just the positive is that all are young boys, young blood, so everyone plays together," Kartik stated.Rajasthan enter the fixture holding a distinct psychological edge from their previous outing, while Railways arrive looking to bounce back hard after conceding a first-innings lead to Uttarakhand.For Kartik and his youthful troops, the overarching objective remains focused on the ultimate prize. "The target is to win as many matches as possible," Kartik concluded.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘We've matched the defending champions’: West Indies head coach Daren Sammy after 2-2 India T20I draw
articles.summary: West Indies head coach Daren Sammy believes his team has taken a major step forward after drawing the five-match T20I series 2-2 against India.
articles.body: West Indies head coach Daren Sammy believes his team has taken a major step forward after drawing the five-match T20I series 2-2 against India. The final match in Bengaluru was abandoned due to rain, but Sammy said the team's performances showed that the players are regaining confidence and can compete with the world's best sides.Sammy also highlighted the need for greater financial support to help West Indies cricket grow and maintain its place in international cricket.Sammy sees confidence returning to West IndiesSammy said West Indies had entered the series with many people doubting their chances against India. However, the players proved they could challenge the reigning T20 world champions on their home ground."It's a true reflection of how all the teams have played, especially for our guys. I'm pretty sure when the series started, we probably didn't have a chance. But that was just the opinion of others. We would want to win because of something we've not done forever in India, so it would have been nice. I think the cup still is in our favour because we won the home leg the last time we played (in 2023) 3-2,” Sammy told reporters in the post-match press conference.He added that the team's ability to match India and outperform them in certain areas showed how much progress the players had made.“We understand what success means to us; we don't ever take for granted where we are as a team and the challenges that we face. We just look to make those strides, and I think after this series we've taken a massive step. We played against the defending champions, and we've matched them (and) in certain areas we've outplayed them, especially in their backyard,” he added.Sammy calls for financial supportBeyond the team's results, Sammy stressed that West Indies cricket needs financial backing to secure its future. He pointed to the sport's rich history in the Caribbean and its contribution to fans and businesses around the world.He said the team's recent performances could help attract the support needed to strengthen the regional game.“I think it's important; my mom always says you must have a care factor. No matter what you do in life, the human nature should never lose that care factor. I think we're in a position where we need somebody to put a (hand around the shoulder) of the West Indies cricket. Financially, that is, and series like this, here in India, against the best team in the world, puts us in a conversation closer to that,” he said.Sammy also welcomed the renewed confidence and fighting spirit among his players.“All the guys in the dressing room, they've gone out there and played with intent and I think what was good to see is that the swagger is back, the confidence is back. It started during the World Cup and you could see guys enjoying, and there was a willingness to win. That's where it starts; the belief that we belong where we are, and to have the performances that says you belong there. Hopefully, right now it's just been consistent,” he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘No option but to bat at 5 or 6’: Tilak Varma on adapting to new role in India’s T20I setup
articles.summary: India vice-captain Tilak Varma has acknowledged that moving away from his preferred No.
articles.body: India vice-captain Tilak Varma has acknowledged that moving away from his preferred No. 3 position to bat lower down the order presents a challenge, but the 23-year-old is confident that regular practice and mental preparation will help him adjust to the demands of his new role.Tilak has increasingly been used at No. 5 and 6 in T20Is as India continue to settle on their batting combination. While the Hyderabad batter admits that he finds it easier to bat higher up the order, he is focused on becoming a reliable finisher for the team.Speaking after the fifth and final T20I against the West Indies was washed out on Saturday night, Tilak said adapting to different batting positions requires considerable work, particularly when the responsibility is to close out games."It's not that easy to change the numbers from 3 to 5 and 6. It will be slightly challenging. But I have been working on that. How can I finish the games? I have said that I love finishing the games for the country," he said."So, for me as an individual, if you see, it will be easier batting at 3. But unfortunately, now I should bat at 5 or 6 because we have got that combination at the top right now."The left-hander's record at No. 6 offers encouragement. Across nine matches in that position, he averages 65.66 at a strike rate of 195. In 26 combined innings at Nos. 5 and 6, he has scored at an average of 46 and a strike rate of 158.However, the arrival of Ishan Kishan, captain Shreyas Iyer's presence at No. 4 and the management's decision to continue with the Abhishek Sharma-Sanju Samson opening combination have left Tilak with a reduced role in the middle order.Kishan has been batting at No. 3 and has impressed in the position, leaving Tilak with little choice but to embrace the finishing responsibilities."Kishan is batting at number 3 now, and he is batting really brilliantly there. So, for me now, I think there is no option but to bat at 5 and 6 and do the job for the team."So, I am mentally prepared for that role. And if you see the last few games, I have won from there. So, I am pretty confident to do well there as well," he added.Tilak working on his finishing skillsTilak said he has been putting in extra work in the nets to expand his shot-making range and improve his ability to score quickly when batting with limited time at the crease.He explained that players operating at Nos. 5 and 6 often have only five or six overs to make an impact, making it important to capitalise on scoring opportunities, including when bowlers deliver slower balls within their hitting range."Yeah, we should do that, otherwise, it will be slightly tough. When you go in to bat as a finisher, if a slower one comes into your arc, you should go for 6. Otherwise, if you see in T20, most of the time, if you go into that role of 5 or 6, you will get a maximum of 5 to 6 overs to bat."So, I have changed personally. I have been in this role in my childhood as well. I have got the shots going all over the ground. So, I am confident that if I bat at 3 or 5, I have got the technique to adapt. So, if I practise for 1 or 2 days, I can do any role for the team."Now, if I come back to No. 3, I can adapt after a day or two of practice. I am confident of batting anywhere," he noted.Busy schedule no excuse, says India vice-captainIndia's players have endured a packed run of fixtures over the past few months, travelling across the United Kingdom, Japan and India. The team will soon head to New Zealand for an all-format tour.Tilak admitted that the demands of consecutive series, different time zones and changing conditions can be difficult, particularly for younger players. However, he stressed that handling such challenges is part of playing international cricket."It will be slightly challenging. But as professional cricketers, we can't give any excuse because when we play back-to-back series, there will be different time zones and all those things. We are used to it now. If you see, for any youngster coming into the team, it will be slightly challenging."But again, you are playing for the country and at the highest level. So, as I said, you should be mentally strong enough to prepare for any challenge, any conditions so that you can become a bigger player," he added.Tilak highlights positives from West Indies seriesDespite the challenges, Tilak believes India have several encouraging takeaways from the West Indies series that they can carry into the upcoming assignments in New Zealand.He pointed to the team's consistent run-scoring, with India crossing the 200-run mark in every match, as a major positive. He also acknowledged the contributions of Nitish Reddy, Shivam Dube and Naman Dhir."There have been quite a few good things. Especially in the batting, every game we have scored over 200 plus. So, that's a big positive, and that too, we haven't got a proper all-rounder in the team. We have played both Nitish (Reddy) and (Shivam) Dubey as well. But both have done decently well."Then Naman (Dhir) bowled well under pressure. As an off-spinner, bowling to right-handers, and that too against a big-gun team like the West Indies."So, there are a few good points for us to take into the upcoming series. As a team, we have introspected a few things in the bowling as well. So, hopefully, we will do well in the New Zealand series," he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘RR are at the top of the list’: Ashwin makes big revelation on Hardik Pandya trade
articles.summary: Speculation surrounding Hardik Pandya's future with Mumbai Indians has intensified, with former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin weighing in on reports
articles.body: Speculation surrounding Hardik Pandya's future with Mumbai Indians has intensified, with former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin weighing in on reports linking the star all-rounder with a potential move to Chennai Super Kings ahead of the next Indian Premier League season.Rumours of a possible trade between the five-time champions have gained traction on social media, with suggestions that CSK icon MS Dhoni could personally persuade Hardik to join the Chennai franchise. However, Ashwin believes that while the all-rounder's arrival would strengthen CSK, a deal remains a distant possibility.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ashwin acknowledged the appeal of having Hardik in the CSK setup but stopped short of endorsing the speculation surrounding the proposed move."There have been conversations that Dhoni will personally convince Hardik Pandya to come to CSK. It will be a great addition for CSK. But in my opinion, it is a real far-shot," said Ashwin.The former India spinner also offered an alternative possibility, claiming that Rajasthan Royals could be better placed to secure Hardik's services if a trade materialises."From what I've heard, RR are at the top of the list in the Hardik trade," he added.Ashwin's comments come at a crucial time for Mumbai Indians, who are preparing for a significant change in their coaching setup following the departure of head coach Mahela Jayawardene.Mahela Jayawardene leaves Mumbai Indians after second stintMumbai Indians confirmed on Saturday that Jayawardene had ended his second spell as head coach after two seasons in charge.The 49-year-old Sri Lankan, who guided the franchise to three IPL titles during his first tenure, returned to the role ahead of the 2025 season after previously coaching MI between 2017 and 2022.His second stint produced mixed results. Mumbai finished fourth in the 2025 season before suffering defeat in Qualifier 2, while their 2026 campaign proved considerably more disappointing, with the five-time champions ending the tournament in ninth place.The franchise must now identify a new head coach with the November 15 IPL retention deadline less than a month away.With a major decision pending in the dugout and trade speculation surrounding Hardik continuing, Mumbai Indians face an important period ahead of the next season.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Hardik Pandya is irreplaceable': Sunil Gavaskar believes India should stop searching for a direct replacement for all-rounder
articles.summary: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar believes India should stop searching for a direct replacement for Hardik Pandya, as the all-rounder brings a unique
articles.body: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar believes India should stop searching for a direct replacement for Hardik Pandya, as the all-rounder brings a unique combination of batting and bowling that is difficult to match.Instead, he advised the team to consider players who can perform different roles while maintaining a strong bowling attack.Gavaskar shared his views after India's five-match T20I series against the West Indies ended in a 2-2 draw. The final match in Bengaluru was abandoned due to rain.Gavaskar wants India to strengthen its bowlingGavaskar suggested that India should play at least four specialist bowlers and use all-rounders as the fifth and sixth bowling options. He warned that selecting too many batters could weaken the bowling unit and cost India matches."We sometimes get a little bit carried away with trying to find a replacement for Hardik Pandya. Hardik Pandya is irreplaceable. If you can't find somebody of his calibre, then go with somebody who will do a slightly different job," Gavaskar said on JioStar.He pointed to Naman Dhir as an example of a player who can contribute with both bat and ball. Dhir scored an unbeaten 24 off just six balls in the rain-hit final T20I."Naman Dhir is doing that job. He's bowling his overs well, and look at the way he batted in this game," he said.Gavaskar also highlighted the importance of backing spin bowlers and helping them maintain confidence, even when they are not regular members of the playing XI."The moment you go with batting up to number eight, you weaken your bowling, and that's where you get beaten," he said.Chopra assesses Abhishek Sharma's performanceGavaskar added that the abandoned final denied India a chance to assess their bowling in the shortened match.Former India opener Aakash Chopra also reviewed Abhishek Sharma's performance, saying the left-handed batter was not at his usual best during the series. However, he stressed that inconsistent performances are normal in an aggressive batting approach."In the last game, when he didn't get much strike, he looked a bit scratchy. He didn't get any rhythm at all, and let's discount whatever happened in this game. So, he was a bit below par by his standards in the series, but that is also going to happen."Chopra added that players aiming for strike rates around 200 cannot be expected to score consistently in every match.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shubman Gill scores just one run on Ranji Trophy return ahead of New Zealand Tests
articles.summary: Shubman Gill had a disappointing return to domestic red-ball cricket, scoring just one run for Punjab against Chhattisgarh in their Ranji Trophy Elite
articles.body: Shubman Gill had a disappointing return to domestic red-ball cricket, scoring just one run for Punjab against Chhattisgarh in their Ranji Trophy Elite Group B match in New Chandigarh on Sunday.The India Test captain is using the domestic competition to prepare for the upcoming two-match Test series against New Zealand.Gill came in to bat at No. 4 after Vihaan Malhotra was dismissed on the first ball of the 26th over. However, his innings lasted only five deliveries.Chhattisgarh bowler Ajay Mandal bowled him on the third ball of the 27th over, leaving Punjab at 68/3. Gill managed just one run, which came off the second ball he faced.Gill prepares for New Zealand TestsGill was added to Punjab's squad at the last minute to get some red-ball match practice before India's Test series against New Zealand, which begins on November 19.Before joining the Test preparations, Gill is expected to play in the first three ODIs of India's five-match series against New Zealand, scheduled from November 4 to 15. His deputy, Shreyas Iyer, will take over as ODI captain after Gill leaves to prepare for the Tests.Despite his early dismissal in the Ranji Trophy, Gill has enjoyed an impressive year in international cricket. In three Tests this year, he has scored 200 runs in four innings at an average of 50.00, including one century and one half-century.Impressive international formGill has been particularly successful in limited-overs cricket. Across 15 international matches this year, he has scored 1,095 runs at an average of 91.25, with four centuries and six half-centuries in 15 innings.His highest score during this run was an unbeaten 223 against the West Indies in the second ODI. With the New Zealand Test series approaching, Gill will be looking to regain his touch in the coming matches and lead India in the crucial red-ball contest.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Consistency is overrated in T20s’: Former India cricketer explains fine line between form and failure
articles.summary: Former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara believes consistency is overrated for top-order batters in T20 cricket, backing Sanju Samson to regain form with one
articles.body: Former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara believes consistency is overrated for top-order batters in T20 cricket, backing Sanju Samson to regain form with one good innings ahead of India's upcoming multi-format tour of New Zealand."Consistency should be there, but for the top order, I think consistency is overrated in T20s," Pujara said while analysing Samson's fluctuating returns on JioHotstar's 'Out or Not Out', as quoted by news agency PTI."He is never out of form. The kind of player Sanju Samson has been in the T20 format; his form fluctuates. But it is always a matter of one innings. He plays one good innings, and he is back in form.""So, you cannot say that this player is not in form. In the T20 format, you are bound to have failures. Who doesn't get out in T20s?" he added.India recently ended their five-match T20I series against the West Indies in a 2-2 draw. They will begin their multi-format tour of New Zealand with the shortest format.Pujara also expressed doubts over whether Samson and teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi could feature together in India's playing XI in New Zealand. He said the conditions could require more all-rounders, leaving less room for specialist batters in the top order."Vaibhav playing every game seems a bit difficult in New Zealand because there you need more all-rounders, either a spin all-rounder or a seaming all-rounder. So, there you don't need a lot of batters, especially in the top order," he said."Either Sanju Samson can open or Vaibhav. I don't think both can be part of the playing XI in New Zealand conditions. So, Vaibhav will have to wait, but he will get opportunities."However, Pujara said Sooryavanshi could still get a chance if the conditions or a player's fitness opened up a spot in the team."If the spot opens up for him based on conditions or players' fitness, that's fine. But both Sanju and Vaibhav cannot be in the playing XI in New Zealand," he said.Former India assistant coach Abhishek Nayar also backed Samson, saying the wicketkeeper-batter's place in the team would come under scrutiny after a few quiet games, but one big innings could silence the questions."Sanju plays with everyone's emotions because he won't score runs for two matches, and everyone starts raising questions," Nayar said.Nayar added that Sooryavanshi might have to wait for his opportunities, with team balance and the need for a left-right batting combination likely to influence India's selection decisions.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Nahida Akter replaces Nigar Sultana as Bangladesh's new T20I captain, Sobhana Mostary named deputy
articles.summary: Nahida Akter has been appointed Bangladesh's new T20I captain, with the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) confirming the decision to Cricbuzz on Sunday.
articles.body: Nahida Akter has been appointed Bangladesh's new T20I captain, with the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) confirming the decision to Cricbuzz on Sunday. Nahida succeeds Nigar Sultana, who stepped down from the role following the Asian Games to focus on her game. Sobhana Mostary has been named vice-captain of the side.Nahida Akter Takes Over T20I Leadership“We sat with members of the selection panel along with others and decided to hand over the T20I captaincy to Nahida. Sobhana Mostary will be her deputy,” Rafiqul told Cricbuzz on Sunday.The board believes Nahida's experience in the leadership group makes her the right choice to lead the T20I team. The left-arm spinner had served as Bangladesh's vice-captain since Sultana was appointed captain in 2022.“Nahida has been the vice-captain for a pretty long time and now we feel the time is right to give her the responsibility of our T20I squad,” Rafiqul added.Nigar Sultana to Continue as Bangladesh's ODI CaptainSultana's decision to relinquish the T20I captaincy will not affect her role in the 50-over format. The wicketkeeper-batter will continue to lead Bangladesh in ODIs, having captained the team during their recent three-match tour of Australia.The BCB was reportedly caught off guard by Sultana's decision. It is understood that the former T20I captain was disappointed with the way she had been treated by the board in recent times, prompting her to step away from the leadership role in the shortest format.Bangladesh's Next AssignmentBangladesh's next assignment will be the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy in Thailand, where their campaign is scheduled to begin against Pakistan on November 12. articles.title: Ian Botham reopens war of words with Ben Stokes over Ashes fallout
articles.summary: England lost the last Ashes series 4-1 and Ian Botham criticised England's preparation for the series; Ben Stokes said that 'has-beens' did not have the same factors at play as his England side did when they got ready for the Ashes
articles.body:
The pair have criticised each other in the media in the past year following England's poor performance in the Ashes in Australia.

Botham criticised England's lack of preparation ahead of the Ashes series last winter, which led to Stokes calling him and Michael Vaughan "has-beens".

England lost the series 4-1 amid off-the-field issues over late-night drinking sessions and breached curfews.

Botham, who scored 5,200 runs and took 383 wickets in 102 Tests, was asked whether he liked the way Stokes resigned as captain in the middle of a Test match against New Zealand.

"No, I didn't and I stand by what I said," Botham said.

"You have got a situation, starting from the beginning when he had a go at myself and Michael Vaughan in Melbourne because we said they had not prepared properly.

"They played two and a half days of cricket in the build-up to taking on Australia in Perth.

"But to be absolutely honest with you, we had a go at them saying that's ridiculous, no one knows what they are doing, the slip fielders have to practice, very, very difficult."

When Stokes was asked by journalists for his views on the criticisms, he replied: "We've not been preparing for this tour over the last three weeks, we've put a lot of thought and process into this for a few years now.

"There's quite a few factors that play into why we can't prepare how the has-beens maybe prepared in the past."

Botham, who was part of two victorious tours of Australia in 1978-79 and 1986-87, was speaking at the Cheltenham Literature Festival to promote his new book, Seasons.

"So that's open warfare and I'm quite happy with that because I just think he let himself down," Botham said.

"He's a bloody good cricketer and he played well but he let himself down in those final couple of months.

"The team going 2-0 down in Australia, one of them in two days.

"For me to be then seen at Noosa, one of the most popular places in Australia to holiday and, we have got five days off on the lash.

"I just thought that was poor. Curfews, well, they were set and they were broken.

"In the book, I just said that right at the end, a throw away line, 'Well, well, well, Ben Stokes, you are now a member of the has-been team'.

"Didn't go down too well, not that I'm bothered."

Botham said that during the Ashes tour of 1986-87, which England won 2-1, the players would go to Australian wineries to drink and socialise between matches.

"That's out of visual and we were actually winning, so we could have paraded ourselves around a bit if we wanted, but we didn't," Botham added.

articles.title: Mohammad Rizwan gets first relief in PCB inquiry, allowed to resume domestic cricket
articles.summary: Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan has been cleared to return to domestic cricket amid an ongoing inquiry into allegations involving online
articles.body: Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan has been cleared to return to domestic cricket amid an ongoing inquiry into allegations involving online betting, gambling and the leaking of dressing-room information. The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has permitted him to feature in the ongoing Presidents Cup first-class tournament, offering the veteran batter a reprieve as the investigation continues.Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Hafeez, who serves as director and head coach of Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL), confirmed that he had received an email from the PCB's domestic department authorising Rizwan to play from October 19.The fifth round of the tournament began on Monday, with Rizwan expected to captain the SNGPL side, Hafeez said.Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq Were Called Back From EnglandRizwan and fellow Pakistan batter Imam-ul-Haq were barred from domestic cricket after being called back from England following the second Test in August. Both players were asked to face an inquiry by the National Cyber Crime Cell (NCCA) over alleged leaks of dressing-room information and issues related to online betting and gambling.Rizwan has appeared before the agency twice for questioning. However, the exact nature of the complaints being investigated by the government body remains unclear.The phones belonging to Rizwan and Imam were also seized by security personnel accompanying the Pakistan team during the second Test at Lord's. The devices remain with the NCCA for forensic examination as part of the inquiry.Inquiry Could Be Concluded SoonWhile Imam has largely remained out of the public eye, Rizwan has continued to attract attention amid the investigation. However, a reliable source indicated on Sunday that the situation had largely eased following the wicketkeeper-batter's most recent session with the NCCA on October 10 in Lahore.The source also suggested that the inquiry could be concluded soon, although no official announcement confirming its closure has been made.The PCB's decision to allow Rizwan to resume domestic cricket marks a significant development in the matter. However, permission to play should not be interpreted as confirmation that the inquiry has been concluded or that the allegations have been resolved.Rizwan Returns After Lengthy Absence From Competitive CricketRizwan, who has represented Pakistan in 47 Tests, 103 ODIs and 106 T20 Internationals, has not played competitive cricket since the second Test against England at Lord's.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: The opening day of the Ranji Trophy witnessed impressive bowling performances from Mumbai pacer Tushar Deshpande who claimed four wickets to put their Mumbai in commanding positions. articles.title: South Africa stutter on rain-wrecked day against Australia in second Test as Scott Boland takes two wickets in two balls
articles.summary: Scott Boland dismisses Aiden Markram and David Bedingham from successive deliveries as South Africa close on 20-2 from 12.2 overs possible around the rain in  Gqeberha; Australia - who left out premier spinner Nathan Lyon - lead three-Test series 1-0 after 214-run win in Durban
articles.body:
Boland, selected in Gqeberha as Australia omitted off-spinner Nathan Lyon and went in with a four-pronged pace attack, bowled Aiden Markam (11) off an inside edge in the ninth over before then nicking off David Bedingham (0) with his next delivery.

South Africa, 1-0 down in the three-match series after a 214-run defeat in the opening game at Durban, were 12-2 at that stage having been put into bat but reached the premature stumps without any further casualties as debutant Marques Ackerman (5no off 32 balls) and captain Temba Bavuma (4no off 13) battled.

Rain meant play started around two hours later than scheduled and it returned to bring about an early lunch after just 5.3 overs before another downpour led to the day being abandoned at 4.15pm local time at St George's Park.

Boland for Lyon was Australia's only change from the first match, with the Baggy Greens leaving their premier spinner out of a red-ball Test in which he was fit to play for the first time since 2013.

South Africa made three alterations with left-arm spinner Keshav Maharaj, wicketkeeper Kyle Verreynne and batter Tristan Stubbs axed for batters Ackerman and Matthew Breetzke and fit-again paceman Kagiso Rabada.

Ryan Rickelton took the wicketkeeping gloves in Verreynne's absence and dropped down from his opening position to No 6, with Ackerman coming in to partner Markam at the top of the order.

Ackerman, 30, was opening in a first-class match for the first time and dug in on a seam-friendly wicket.

articles.body: Faheem Ashraf pulled off a relay catch to break Sri Lanka's opening partnership in the ODI Tri-Series match against Pakistan after debutant wicketkeeper Saad Baig failed to hold on to the ball.Pakistan had posted 305 runs after batting first, and Sri Lanka made a steady start to their chase with a 30-run opening stand. articles.title: Shafali Verma scripts history with ninth 50-plus score as India thrash Zimbabwe to seal T20I series
articles.summary: Shafali Verma continued her prolific run in women’s T20 internationals, smashing a 25-ball 55 as India thrashed Zimbabwe by nine wickets in the second
articles.body: Shafali Verma continued her prolific run in women’s T20 internationals, smashing a 25-ball 55 as India thrashed Zimbabwe by nine wickets in the second T20I to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series on Sunday.The Indian opener set a new benchmark for the most 50-plus scores by a batter in a calendar year in women’s T20Is, registering her ninth such innings in 2026. She moved past Smriti Mandhana, who recorded eight 50-plus scores in 2024, while Mithali Raj and Hong Kong’s Natasha Miles have seven and eight, respectively, in 2018 and 2026.Shafali’s latest half-century, her 22nd in T20Is, came as India chased down Zimbabwe’s modest target of 103 in just 8.5 overs after restricting the visitors to 102/8.Most 50-plus scores in a calendar year9 - Shafali Verma (IND-W) in 20268 - Smriti Mandhana (IND-W) in 20247 - Mithali Raj (IND-W) in 20187 - Natasha Miles (HKG-W) in 2026Shafali-Mandhana partnership adds to record yearShafali and captain Smriti Mandhana combined to make short work of the chase, sharing a 96-run opening partnership that put India firmly in control. Mandhana remained unbeaten on 47, while Shafali’s aggressive knock featured sixes and boundaries that left Zimbabwe’s bowlers struggling for answers.The stand also extended the pair’s remarkable record in 2026. Shafali and Mandhana have now registered nine 50-plus partnerships in women’s T20Is this calendar year, the most by any pair. They surpassed their own tally of seven such stands in 2024 and moved ahead of Hong Kong’s Yasmin Daswani and Natasha Miles, who have eight in 2026.Most 50-plus stands in a calendar year in Women’s T20Is (any wicket)9 - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma (IND-W) in 20268 - Yasmin Daswani, Natasha Miles (HKG-W) in 20267 - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma (IND-W) in 2024Shafali reached her half-century in 26 balls, taking on off-spinner Beloved Biza for a six. She also punished Michelle Mavunga with three consecutive deliveries yielding four, four and six. Mandhana, meanwhile, struck four successive boundaries against pacer Nyasha Gwanzura before finishing the chase with an inside-out six off Olinder Chare.The victory also gave Mandhana a series win at the start of her full-time captaincy stint.India’s bowlers restrict Zimbabwe to 102/8Earlier, India’s bowlers delivered a disciplined performance to prevent Zimbabwe from building momentum after the visitors opted to bat first. Nandani Sharma dismissed opener Kelis Ndhlovu for a duck, and Zimbabwe managed only 20 runs in the powerplay. articles.summary: For Gurjapneet Singh, a strong performance in domestic cricket is only another step towards a bigger goal.
articles.body: For Gurjapneet Singh, a strong performance in domestic cricket is only another step towards a bigger goal. The Tamil Nadu left-arm pacer made an immediate impact against Uttarakhand in the Ranji Trophy, claiming four wickets on the opening day, but insisted that his job would remain unfinished until he earns a chance to represent India.Playing just his 10th first-class match, Gurjapneet returned figures of 4/34 as Tamil Nadu bowled out Uttarakhand, last season’s semi-finalists, for 134 in their Elite Group D clash at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai.“There is no satisfaction unless I play for India. That's the main job, and that box is still empty. I have to tick that,” Gurjapneet told reporters at the end of the first day's play.The 26-year-old, who represents Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in the IPL and is part of the BCCI's targeted pool of fast bowlers, missed Tamil Nadu's previous match against Rajasthan in Jaipur while representing India A in the 50-over series against Australia in Puducherry.Gurjapneet makes early inroads with the new ballOperating with the new ball on a red-soil surface affected by heavy overnight rain, Gurjapneet struck early to put Uttarakhand on the back foot. He dismissed Aarav Mahajan before trapping Dega Nischal leg-before-wicket and removing Kunal Chandela during an incisive opening spell. He also troubled India Under-19 batter Lakshya Raichandani before returning to dismiss Uttarakhand's top-scorer, Avneesh Sudha, for 54 and complete his four-wicket haul.Gurjapneet attributed his success to reading the batters and adjusting his angles rather than sticking to a fixed plan.“It is just instinct. I watch his feet movement and how he is reacting. One ball I bowl from over the stumps and later I come around the stumps. Maybe his conscious mind is ready to play from that angle, and the results were positive,” he explained.Managing workload after India A stintHaving battled injuries in the past, Gurjapneet has also focused on preparing his body for the demands of red-ball cricket after switching from the shorter format.“I was practising a lot with both balls. Coming into the Ranji Trophy, the workload is high and you have to keep maintaining that,” he said.He added that managing his fitness and energy levels was crucial to bowling long spells without overexerting himself.“I'm just trying to keep that energy the same because I know in red-ball cricket, it's difficult to bowl long spells. I'm trying to keep my body ready for all spells and deliver that.”Bowling to India's stars boosts confidenceGurjapneet's experience as a net bowler with the Indian team has helped strengthen his belief in his abilities. Bowling to established international batters such as Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli, he said, gave him confidence that he could carry into domestic cricket.He has also benefited from conversations with India bowling coach Morne Morkel, who advised him to focus on his lengths and keep varying his angles.“He just said you have good skills and to keep focusing on your length and keep changing angles,” Gurjapneet recalled.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mohammad Rizwan gets first relief in PCB inquiry, allowed to resume domestic cricket
articles.summary: Mohammad Rizwan has been granted approval by the Pakistan Cricket Board to rejoin domestic cricket amidst ongoing investigations into allegations of online b...
articles.body:
Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan has been cleared to return to domestic cricket amid an ongoing inquiry into allegations involving online betting, gambling and the leaking of dressing-room information. The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has permitted him to feature in the ongoing Presidents Cup first-class tournament, offering the veteran batter a reprieve as the investigation continues. Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Hafeez, who serves as director and head coach of Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL), confirmed that he had received an email from the PCB's domestic department authorising Rizwan to play from October 19. The fifth round of the tournament began on Monday, with Rizwan expected to captain the SNGPL side, Hafeez said.

Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq Were Called Back From England

Rizwan and fellow Pakistan batter Imam-ul-Haq were barred from domestic cricket after being called back from England following the second Test in August. Both players were asked to face an inquiry by the National Cyber Crime Cell (NCCA) over alleged leaks of dressing-room information and issues related to online betting and gambling. Rizwan has appeared before the agency twice for questioning. However, the exact nature of the complaints being investigated by the government body remains unclear. The phones belonging to Rizwan and Imam were also seized by security personnel accompanying the Pakistan team during the second Test at Lord's. The devices remain with the NCCA for forensic examination as part of the inquiry.

While Imam has largely remained out of the public eye, Rizwan has continued to attract attention amid the investigation. However, a reliable source indicated on Sunday that the situation had largely eased following the wicketkeeper-batter's most recent session with the NCCA on October 10 in Lahore. The source also suggested that the inquiry could be concluded soon, although no official announcement confirming its closure has been made. The PCB's decision to allow Rizwan to resume domestic cricket marks a significant development in the matter. However, permission to play should not be interpreted as confirmation that the inquiry has been concluded or that the allegations have been resolved.

Rizwan Returns After Lengthy Absence From Competitive Cricket

Rizwan, who has represented Pakistan in 47 Tests, 103 ODIs and 106 T20 Internationals, has not played competitive cricket since the second Test against England at Lord's.

articles.title: Pakistan defeat Sri Lanka in opening game of ODI tri-series as captain Salman Ali Agha makes triumphant return
articles.summary: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by 37 runs to win the opening match of the ODI tri-series; Pakistan captain Salman Ali Agha returned to score a century; Watch England's first game against Pakistan in Rawalpindi on Tuesday, live on Sky Sports from 9am
articles.body:
Agha top-scored with 107 off 90 balls as Pakistan were bowled out for 305 in 49.5 overs after Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis won his fourth successive toss and elected to field.

The batsman was among seven Pakistan cricketers summoned home at the end of August during a turbulent tour of England, having captained the side in the first Test.

Pakistan pace bowlers overcame heavy dew and threatening half centuries from Pavan Rathnayake (79) and Janith Liyanage (60) to dismiss Sri Lanka for 268 in 48.1 overs.

Captain Shaheen Afridi picked up three for 55 while Naseem Shah pinned down Sri Lanka's top-order with impressive swing bowling to finish on two for 43. Haris Rauf ran through the tail with two for 48 while seam all-rounder Faheem Ashraf grabbed two for 49, including the key wicket of Rathnayake.

Avishka Fernando, making a comeback to ODIs, top-edged Shah while Kusal Mendis struggled for 34 balls to score only 18 before he fell to Ashraf.

Kamindu Mendis (44 in 50) survived two dropped catches before Afridi struck twice in his return spell as Sri Lanka limped to 91-4 in the 20th over of its chase.

Rathnayake and Liyanage then revived Sri Lankan hopes with a 119-run stand with Pakistan pacers unable to reverse swing the wet ball due to heavy dew at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.

But the dismissal of Rathnayake in the 38th over provided Pakistan an opening despite Dasun Shanaka, playing his first ODI since the start of 2024, scoring 28 off 18 balls.

After being summoned home, Agha was stripped of the Pakistan T20 captaincy and dropped from the side that beat Sri Lanka 2-1 in their recent three-match series. However, a prolific run of domestic form, including a triple century, earned him a recall to the ODI team.

Agha helped Pakistan recover from 118-4 in the 22nd over, building crucial partnerships with Hasan Nawaz (37) and Arafat Minhas (18), before Sri Lanka struck back in the death overs.

Eshan Malinga (4-46) and Asitha Fernando (3-59) struck repeatedly in the final five overs to deny Pakistan a strong finish. From 279-5, Pakistan lost its last five wickets for just 26 runs. Malinga claimed two wickets in a maiden over before No. 11 Haris Rauf denied him a hat-trick.

Dilshan Madushanka (2-67) removed openers Fakhar Zaman (16) and Saim Ayub (7) in his opening spell.

Babar Azam and 19-year-old debutant Saad Baig rebuilt with a 74-run third-wicket stand before Malinga removed both batters in successive overs.

Babar, who has scored just one ODI century in more than two years, fell for 45 off 57 balls, pulling a short delivery from Malinga straight to mid-wicket. Baig struck two sixes and three fours before falling to the same bowler, mistiming a pull to deep fine leg.

Agha wrested back the momentum with a 97-run partnership with Nawaz. Sri Lanka's only specialist leg-spinner, Sachindu Colombage (0-61), struggled to contain them as Agha reached his half-century off 48 balls and Nawaz also attacked.

Fernando returned to break the stand, with Rathnayake taking an excellent catch above his head at mid-wicket to dismiss Nawaz.

Agha continued to attack in a 64-run partnership with Minhas before bringing up his century with an edged boundary.

Pakistan will play England in Rawalpindi on Tuesday in the second match of the tri-series. Watch live on Sky Sports from 9am.

articles.title: ‘He should not play all three formats’: Ravi Shastri’s advice for Jasprit Bumrah
articles.summary: New Delhi: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri has welcomed Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to the T20I squad for the New Zealand tour and believes fellow
articles.body: New Delhi: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri has welcomed Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to the T20I squad for the New Zealand tour and believes fellow veteran Mohammed Shami has done enough to earn a recall in the longer white-ball and red-ball formats.India begin a demanding New Zealand tour on October 22, featuring five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests.“There is no substitute for experience,” Shastri told TOI. “When you have a bowler of Bhuvneshwar’s quality and experience, it’s a no-brainer. With the form he showed in the IPL and his years with India, he’ll be ideal for New Zealand conditions.”Shastri was equally emphatic about Shami’s case for a comeback.“He’s done enough with both red and white balls to be recalled to the Test and ODI sides,” he said.While advocating the return of experienced campaigners, Shastri stressed that India must carefully manage Jasprit Bumrah’s workload in the build-up to the 2027 ODI World Cup.“I don’t think he should play all three formats until the World Cup. He should focus primarily on Test cricket and feature sporadically in ODIs and T20Is. I’d rather preserve him for the two Tests in New Zealand, where he’ll be crucial,” he said.Shastri believes the six-week New Zealand tour could serve as an important benchmark for Indian cricket, particularly with South Africa set to host the 2027 ODI World Cup.“The entire tour is important. It will give a clear indication of where Indian cricket is heading. Conditions there could also mirror some of what India might face in South Africa during the World Cup,” he said.India’s World Test Championship hopes, however, remain a steep challenge.“For India, qualifying for the final is an uphill task. They probably need to win around 90 per cent of their remaining games, including both Tests in New Zealand and at least four of the five against Australia. It’s not impossible, but a lot depends on other results as well,” Shastri said.He expects New Zealand’s conditions to pose a stern examination for India’s batting.“New Zealand will be coming out of winter, so the pitches should be fresh and conducive to seam and swing. The ball will move in the air and off the surface, and the wind can make things even tougher. India will have to adapt quickly.”According to Shastri, partnerships will be vital because wickets can tumble in clusters in those conditions.Test captain Shubman Gill faces a significant leadership test, though Shastri backed the No. 4 batter to cope.“It’s a massive challenge for a young captain, but Gill is in prime form and has always done well in New Zealand. He knows the conditions.”On Rishabh Pant, Shastri’s advice remains simple.“I’ve never told Pant anything other than this: be smart. He has immense ability and shouldn’t change his natural game. Just remain aware of the match situation.”For all the discussion around batting and bowling, Shastri identified fielding as India’s biggest concern.“The biggest improvement I want to see is in fielding. It has dipped alarmingly. To win major tournaments, the standards have to be much higher. Consistency in batting and bowling is important, but fielding is the area that worries me the most,” he said.(Watch India’s tour of New Zealand live and exclusively on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV, starting October 22, 2026.)Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘I have had to change my approach’: Tilak Varma on moving down the order
articles.summary: Bengaluru: For Tilak Varma, the number next to his name on the team sheet matters far less than the one on the scoreboard at the end of the match.
articles.body: Bengaluru: For Tilak Varma, the number next to his name on the team sheet matters far less than the one on the scoreboard at the end of the match.The India T20I vice-captain has seen his role evolve considerably in recent months, moving from the top order to the finisher’s role as the team continues to fine-tune its combinations. While adapting to different batting positions is rarely straightforward, the 23-year-old has embraced the challenge and put the team’s needs ahead of personal preference.Having begun his T20I career near the top of the order, Tilak now often finds himself walking in at No. 5 or 6. With Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma opening, Ishan Kishan firmly established at No. 3 and skipper Shreyas Iyer occupying the next slot, opportunities higher up the order have become limited.Rather than viewing it as a setback, Tilak sees it as another responsibility to master.“Ishan is batting brilliantly at No. 3. So, for me, there is no option but to bat at 5 and 6 and do the job for the team. I am mentally prepared for that role and in the last few games, I have won matches from there. So, I am pretty confident,” Tilak said after the rain-hit series decider against the West Indies in Bengaluru on Saturday.The left-hander admitted that the transition from a top-order batter to a finisher has not been without its challenges.“It’s not easy to change from No. 3 to No. 5 or 6. It is slightly challenging. But I have been working on how I can finish games, and I love finishing games for the country,” he said.The demands of batting in the lower middle order are vastly different from those of a top-order role. There is little time to settle in, and the emphasis is on making an immediate impact rather than constructing an innings. Tilak said he has consciously altered his preparation to meet those demands.“I have been working on it in the nets. Otherwise, it becomes tough. When you go in as a finisher and a slower ball comes into your arc, you need to be ready to hit it for six. In T20 cricket, if you bat at No. 5 or 6, you generally get only five or six overs, so I have had to change my approach.”Fortunately for Tilak, batting down the order is not entirely new territory.“I batted lower down the order in my childhood as well. I have shots all around the ground and I am confident in my ability to adapt. articles.summary: Bengaluru: When batters are scoring at 11.46 runs an over, even quality bowling attacks can be made to look ordinary.
articles.body: Bengaluru: When batters are scoring at 11.46 runs an over, even quality bowling attacks can be made to look ordinary. India’s T20I series against the West Indies has exposed the vulnerability of the hosts’ pace unit, with flat pitches, dew and short boundaries proving a punishing combination for bowlers.West Indies’ stunning 250-run chase in Ranchi, completed with nine balls to spare, prompted a stern assessment from India head coach Gautam Gambhir.“These bowlers are our bowlers, not someone else’s bowlers. Their careers are at stake,” he had said, underlining the scrutiny facing the attack.With the exception of Indore, where India successfully defended 223, the bowlers struggled to contain a fearless West Indies batting line-up. While the absence of Jasprit Bumrah and, to an extent, Hardik Pandya has been felt, the bigger concern for the team management is the inconsistency shown by Arshdeep Singh, Mayank Yadav and Prince Yadav.The two young quicks, Mayank and Prince, have alternated between brilliance and waywardness during the series, highlighting the challenges of adjusting to different match situations. The fourth T20I in Hyderabad offered a clear example. India conceded 18 extras, including 13 wides. Arshdeep accounted for six, while Mayank and Prince leaked two and one, respectively. Their attempts to execute wide yorkers and fuller deliveries repeatedly missed the mark, allowing the West Indies batters to maintain the pressure.India’s lack of proven T20 pace-bowling depth has consequently become a talking point. That has put renewed focus on the return of Bhuvneshwar Kumar, whose recall after nearly four years away from the national side could prove timely.The experienced swing bowler has enjoyed a productive run in the IPL, taking 45 wickets across the last two seasons. More importantly, his success has been built on control and execution rather than sheer pace, qualities that India’s younger quicks have often lacked in this series.Conditions, however, have offered little respite to bowlers. High-scoring surfaces and heavy dew have meant that even small lapses have come at a significant cost.As India prepare for a demanding tour of New Zealand, they know the challenges ahead will be very different. The pitches may offer more assistance, but the key question remains whether the bowling group can quickly adapt and improve its consistency.On the eve of the rain-affected series finale in Bengaluru, fast-bowling coach Morne Morkel urged observers to consider the physical and mental demands placed on modern cricketers.“We sometimes forget that mental fatigue plays a big part. We have to manage that and be smart with it. Some of the players went for the Asian Games and then straight into a full series against the West Indies. These guys are also human,” Morkel said.“Execution and skills become better when you’ve recovered, slept well and mentally refreshed. That’s a challenge. articles.body: Jaipur: It was far from an ideal opening Ranji Trophy match for Sachin Yadav, who scored just 1 and 0 against Tamil Nadu last week, but the left-hander did not put a foot wrong on Sunday. The opener expertly negotiated a tricky opening hour of Day One against Railways in Rajasthan's Group ‘D’ fixture at Sawai Man Singh (SMS) Stadium, anchoring the innings to reach his second First-Class century with an unbeaten 115 off 221 balls.The milestone arrived when he deftly pushed a delivery from seamer Adarsh Singh to third man for a sharp single. The moment triggered an ecstatic celebration, a passionate leap into the air, followed by a nod to KL Rahul’s style as he drew a circle on the pitch and firmly stomped his bat right in the centre. Playing in only his fifth First-Class match, the young opener proved exactly why he is highly regarded, striking 15 fours and two sixes.Alongside Karan Lamba, with whom he stitched a partnership of unbeaten 157, Sachin ensured the day’s honours belonged to the hosts. Rajasthan reached 247/2 when stumps were called nearly an hour early due to a hailstorm.Karan, a centurion in the previous match, picked up right where he left off and looked well on his way to another hundred, sitting unbeaten on 89 (122) with nine fours and two sixes.Sachin considers the ground his fortress. “I consider SMS Stadium as my fortress because I made my debut here and a lot of my good knocks have come here. That is why I did that particular celebration which I took from KL Rahul’s books to communicate that this is my place,” he said after the day’s play.The left-hander focused on playing session by session. “The overcast conditions gave the bowlers some initial movement. My strategy was just to bide my time instead of rushing into things,” he said.Earlier, after opting to bat first, Rajasthan received an early reprieve when opener Rohan Rajbhar was dropped off Adarsh Singh in the third over. However, he failed to capitalise on the lifeline, scoring 11 off 34 balls before seamer Kunal Yadav induced a catch to mid-off in the 13th over.One-down batter Sumit Godara’s brief stay was highlighted by two sixes off spinner Toufik Mondal. articles.body: Mohammed Shami’s continued omission from India’s plans has raised fresh questions, with former India cricketer Mohammad Kaif calling for greater transparency from the selectors following the announcement of the squad for the upcoming series in New Zealand.The BCCI announced India’s squads earlier this week for the New Zealand tour, which includes two Tests, five ODIs and five T20Is. However, the absence of the experienced fast bowler from the squad has drawn criticism, particularly in view of his domestic performances and past contributions to the national team.Kaif believes the selectors owe Shami an explanation, given the pacer’s achievements and his crucial role in India’s run to the 2023 ODI World Cup final. Shami finished that tournament as the leading wicket-taker, claiming 24 wickets in just seven matches.“No questions are asked, no BCCI selector explains the decisions, there’s no accountability. You’ve to keep transparency. This is about Mohammed Shami – the player of the 2023 world cup. If he wasn’t there, India would not have reached the final. When Hardik Pandya got injured, Shami came in and didn’t make you feel the absence of a sixth bowler. If Shami wasn’t there, India would’ve been searching for a sixth bowling option. Rohit Sharma took India to the final with five bowlers because Shami was the backup," Kaif said on Cricbuzz.The former India batter also pointed to Shami’s performances in domestic cricket, arguing that the pacer has continued to make a case for himself despite being away from the international setup.“Shami took 22-23 wickets in Indian conditions. So, I feel there has to be some transparency why the decision has been taken. He’s doing everything – playing first-class cricket, Ranji Trophy, taking wickets," he added.Shami last represented India in March 2025 during the Champions Trophy triumph. His most recent Test appearance, meanwhile, came in the World Test Championship final against Australia in June 2023.The fast bowler has since been attempting to regain his place through domestic cricket following an extended absence from the longest format. Concerns over his match fitness have reportedly been a key factor behind the selectors' reluctance to include him in the Test squad, with questions remaining over his ability to withstand the demands of red-ball cricket.Shami has also been bowling short spells in domestic matches, a factor cited in discussions over his omission. Jasprit Bumrah also bowls four-over spells in Test cricket. In England, his workload was being managed and Shubman Gill followed it. If one bowler is being treated in a particular way, then the same can be done for others too. There’s nothing wrong in bowling short spells if you can get the job done. articles.title: Reverse swing in ODIs: How a rule change has changed the game and what impact could it have?
articles.summary: One rule change has changed the face of ODI cricket. BBC Sport looks at its impact, who is benefiting and what it could mean for the future.
articles.body:
England had just been beaten by Sri Lanka in the second one-day international at Headingley and coach Brendon McCullum was speaking to his players in the dressing room.

"The game is slightly different now," he said. "The ball is playing a massive part."

The difference McCullum referenced is reverse swing - the way an older ball moves in the air in the opposite direction to convention.

The playing conditions in ODIs were changed in July 2025, allowing captains to choose after 34 overs which of the two white balls used at either end they would like to use to complete the rest of the innings.

With the chosen ball now able to get older and scruffier, the result has brought a reverse swing renaissance, something which is already having an impact on the format and poses intriguing possibilities for the future less than 12 months out from the next World Cup.

When Sam Curran bowled England to victory with four wickets at the death in the third ODI against India at Lord's in July, he found more than twice as much swing with the old white ball across his final spell than he did at the start of the innings.

A year earlier, Saqib Mahmood found less than half as much swing in an ODI at Cardiff against West Indies at the death compared to the start.

Those are two random examples. Different days, different players, different situations.

The change to using one ball for the last 16 overs was made to help bowlers, and it is having the desired effect.

Half of full deliveries from pace bowlers in the final 10 overs have swung more than one degree since the rule change - a jump from 35% compared to the 18 months prior.

As a result, the economy rates of pace bowlers in the final five overs have dropped from 8.40 runs per over in the period before the change to 7.95 - a small but not insignificant decline.

Pacers' bowling averages have dropped from 19.2 runs per wicket to 18.3 too.

The verdict? Hitting out at the death is not as easy as it once was.

As has always been the case when reverse swing is in play, pacers are bowling fuller and utilising more inswing now the ball is reversing.

Sri Lanka were particularly effective with this against England in the Headingley ODI last month, bowling 69% of deliveries six metres from the stumps or fuller. It helped them close out a 16-run win.

Despite that, England have, statistically at least, benefited most from the rule change, though it should be noted they have taken a significant step forward with their ODI cricket this year. Their numbers may have improved with or without the change.

Their bowling average (from 36.76 to 20.91) and economy rates (from 9.78 to 7.53) at the death have plummeted since July 2025, while their batting run-rate has actually improved (from 8.07 to 9.16).

After defeat in Leeds, McCullum asked his players to "think" about what the changes may mean for their own plans, suggesting tactical switches may follow.

Three days later at The Oval, England progressed from 104-2 to 214-2 in the 10 overs prior to the Sri Lankans picking their preferred ball.

Australia, New Zealand, West Indies, South Africa, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Afghanistan have all scored slower during the death overs since the rule change.

West Indies' death run-rate has dropped by 2.39 runs per over in that time.

As for individual bowlers around the world, Windies quick Alzarri Joseph and South Africa's Lungi Ngidi have benefited from massive jumps in the amount of swing they have been able to find at the death.

Joseph's average amount of swing has increased by 84%, leading to his bowling average dropping from 24.1 to 17.4.

Similarly, Ngidi's bowling average has dropped to 13 and his economy has fallen from 9.34 to six after a 63.3% increase in swing.

Others to see their movement jump include New Zealand's Nathan Smith, Pakistan's Naseem Shah and Bangladesh's Mustafizur - each with varying results.

Shaheen Afridi, Pakistan's captain in this tri-series, is one of the world's best at finding swing at the death (an average of 1.3 degrees since the rule change), although he was swinging it plenty before the change too (1.2).

Shaheen and Naseem in tandem against England on Tuesday could be a fascinating sight.

Jofra Archer is the England bowler finding the most movement late on, with an average degree of 0.97 - an increase of 37%.

What impact might it have on the World Cup?

Reverse swing is not impacting ODIs everywhere in the world - not yet, at least.

The change has been most significant in England, where the ball is swinging 63% more at the death.

There has been a 33% jump in Bangladesh, with matches held in Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Pakistan - relevant for the next two weeks - also featuring significantly more late movement than before.

The increase has been less significant in Australia, where England travel next, however, and in South Africa where the majority of next year's World Cup will be held.

There have only been three ODIs played in South Africa since the rule change, making predictions for next autumn difficult.

While the change has not taken effect there, South African ODIs already have some of the higher levels of movement late in an innings but, at the same time, teams have scored at 7.35 runs per over there in recent years - again on the higher side.

If a spike in reverse swing does come, teams may have to get their scoring done earlier than previously.

Statistics correct prior to ODI tri-series between Pakistan, Sri Lanka and England.

articles.title: Release Vaibhav Sooryavanshi from India squad? ‘It’s heartbreaking, but no other way,’ says ex-cricketer
articles.summary: Former India opener Aakash Chopra believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi faces an uphill battle to break into India’s T20I playing XI, with the team’s established
articles.body: Former India opener Aakash Chopra believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi faces an uphill battle to break into India’s T20I playing XI, with the team’s established top-order options leaving little room for the 15-year-old to feature.Sooryavanshi is part India’s squad for the upcoming five-match T20I series against New Zealand, which begins on November 22. However, the teenager was not given a single opportunity during the recently concluded home series against the West Indies, which ended in a 2-2 draw.Chopra feels the youngster’s absence from the playing XI is primarily a result of the lack of available slots rather than a question of his ability. He suggested that rotating the top-order batters could be a way to give Sooryavanshi opportunities, although he acknowledged that the idea has not found much support.Speaking on his YouTube channel, the former India batter was asked whether Sooryavanshi should replace Tilak Varma in the XI, given the latter’s perceived inconsistency."Vaibhav Sooryavanshi isn't getting chances because a place isn't getting created for him. In whose place should you play him? To be fair, he can play only in place of Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma, or Ishan Kishan," Chopra responded."When three people are doing well, you can't get a chance suddenly. I know it is heartbreaking, but there is no other way. No one is agreeing with the method I am suggesting. You can do a rotation. Give chances to all four of them in rotation," he added.Chopra suggests Ranji Trophy stint if Sooryavanshi remains on benchChopra also argued that keeping Sooryavanshi in the squad without giving him any playing time throughout the series would serve little purpose. In such a situation, he believes the teenager should be released to play in the Ranji Trophy instead.The youngster has made an encouraging start to his T20I career, scoring 246 runs in eight matches at a strike rate of over 186, including two half-centuries. Despite his impressive numbers and reputation for aggressive batting, he has yet to get a consistent opportunity in the current international setup, with the more experienced Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma preferred at the top of the order.‘Shooting arrows at Tilak Varma is not right’Chopra also defended Tilak Varma, disagreeing with the suggestion that the Indian vice-captain has been underperforming and should make way for Sooryavanshi."If you say Tilak Varma doesn't perform at all, then what you are saying is slightly wrong. Tilak Varma struck two centuries when he played at No. 3. After that, he got injured and had a slight problem before the World Cup," he said.The former India opener pointed to Tilak’s contributions in the middle and lower-middle order, arguing that his recent performances should not be overlooked simply because he has not always batted at his preferred position."The World Cup didn't start well, but after that, ever since he became a finisher, he has done a good job, whether you see the performances in the Asian Games or now. The fact is that he has been doing really well in the middle order and the lower-middle order. So I feel shooting arrows at Tilak Varma is not right," Chopra observed.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Salman Ali Agha made a significant addition to Pakistan’s ODI record books with a century against Sri Lanka in the opening match of the ongoing
articles.body: Salman Ali Agha made a significant addition to Pakistan’s ODI record books with a century against Sri Lanka in the opening match of the ongoing tri-series, becoming the country’s most prolific centurion among batters who have regularly featured at No. 5 or lower.The former Pakistan T20I captain struck 107 off 90 balls, including 10 fours and a six, to help the hosts post 305 in 49.5 overs at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Sunday. Pakistan went on to register a 37-run victory after Sri Lanka suffered a dramatic collapse late in their chase.The hundred was Agha’s fourth in 54 ODIs for Pakistan, with all four coming while batting at No. 5 or lower. His latest effort took him past former Pakistan batter Mohammad Yousuf, with whom he had previously shared the national record for the most ODI centuries from those positions.Yousuf scored three hundreds while batting at No. 5 or lower in ODIs. Between 1998 and 2009, he played 114 matches in those positions, establishing himself as one of Pakistan’s most accomplished batters.Agha has now moved ahead of him, with three of his four ODI centuries coming specifically at No. 5. He has achieved that feat in just 33 matches batting in the position, making him the first Pakistani to score three ODI hundreds at No. 5.Before Agha, Yousuf was the only Pakistan batter to have scored multiple ODI centuries at that position, registering two hundreds in 84 matches at No. 5.While Agha has established a new Pakistan record, the overall mark for the most ODI centuries scored at No. 5 or lower remains with England’s Jos Buttler and South Africa’s David Miller.Most ODI 100s as a No. 5 or lower batterPlayerTeam(s)Time spanMatchesRunsBest score100sJos ButtlerEngland2012–20261904,9971508David MillerSouth Africa2010–20261744,6051428MS DhoniIndia, Asia2004–20193018,324139*7Yuvraj SinghIndia, Asia2000–20171744,8701397Both have eight hundreds in those positions. India’s MS Dhoni and Yuvraj Singh finished their ODI careers with seven centuries apiece, while AB de Villiers, Andrew Symonds, Eoin Morgan and Sikandar Raza have six each.Agha’s latest achievement further underlined his growing importance to Pakistan’s middle order, with his century providing the foundation for a competitive total in the series opener.Pakistan capitalise on Sri Lanka’s late collapseAgha’s contribution proved decisive as Pakistan held their nerve to secure the win after Sri Lanka had mounted a strong recovery during the chase.Sri Lanka had slipped to 91/4 in the 20th over but rebuilt their innings through Janith and Pavan Rathnayake, who combined for a 119-run partnership. The increasing dew also appeared to make batting easier, allowing the pair to revive their side’s hopes.Dasun Shanaka added momentum with an attacking 25 off 14 balls. With five wickets still in hand, Sri Lanka needed just 58 runs from the final eight overs and looked well placed to complete the chase.However, the game turned sharply when Janith and Shanaka were dismissed within four deliveries. Pakistan seized the opportunity, removing Sri Lanka’s final five batters for just 15 runs to seal a 37-run victory.Sri Lanka coach Gary Kirsten was visibly frustrated by the manner in which his side surrendered its position after fighting back into contention.Earlier, Agha had also received valuable support from Pakistan’s lower order.
